issues.competing_evidence: Abstract states a 43-MG synchrotron-region field; §4.1 and Table 2 give about 43 G (Table 2: 42.7±0.2 G fast cooling, 20 G slow cooling) and then separately infer a ~15-MG WD polar field at a modeled location. The abstract/body difference is a factor of 10^6. References: BarrettGurwell+25_ARSco; Garnavich+21_ARSco.
issues.why_it_matters: This changes the inferred local field by six orders of magnitude and the extrapolated WD field by two orders; field location and model are not interchangeable.
issues.needed_action: Check for a publisher correction or request author clarification of the abstract unit and the Table 2/body model units. Until then, retain the table/body G result and the abstract MG claim as distinct unresolved entries; do not select a global WD field.

issues.competing_evidence: The 2025 abstract gives Pspin=117.0564 s and a 58.26-s modulation. Its §3.2 gives the periodogram peak 17.053(23) mHz =58.641(79) s and compares it with twice Pelisoli+22 nu_spin=17.0764365689(59) mHz; the 2025 full text elsewhere uses 117.12 s. References: BarrettGurwell+25_ARSco; Pelisoli+22_ARSco.
issues.why_it_matters: An incorrect period could conflate a spin fundamental, a harmonic and the beat; the accepted timing solution makes the 220-GHz peak a near-2-spin harmonic, not a new 58-s spin.
issues.needed_action: Verify abstract numbers against the journal record/corrigendum/authors. Preserve the body periodogram value and published Pelisoli spin/beat clocks separately meanwhile.

issues.competing_evidence: Barrett & Gurwell §3.1 reports mean S220=124±2 mJy, with range 77–167 mJy; Appendix B Table 3 gives 124±10 mJy for SMA 220 GHz. Reference: BarrettGurwell+25_ARSco.
issues.why_it_matters: Flux uncertainty affects spectral-index and SED model constraints, including the inferred field.
issues.needed_action: Check the paper table/text or any erratum/source data to identify statistical versus calibration uncertainty; keep both published entries until resolved.

issues.competing_evidence: Marsh+16 defines q=M2/M1 and q>0.35, with WD allowed mass 0.81–1.29 M_sun. du Plessis+19 uses q=M1/M2 and reports q=3.45(+0.66/-0.45) and MWD=1.00(+0.16/-0.10) M_sun assuming i≈zeta and Roche-lobe filling. du Plessis+22 later finds RVM alpha/zeta fits vary by ~10/~30 degrees over orbital phase. issues.why_it_matters: Mixing inverse q conventions or promoting zeta to orbital i can change mass conclusions and propagate into evolutionary comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Retain the published solutions with explicit conventions and model assumptions. Decide whether the 2019 model mass remains suitable for a preferred catalog field after considering phase-resolved fit behavior; no single mass is selected in the ledger.

issues.competing_evidence: Field claims refer to different components/methods: Garnavich+21 photospheric Ly-alpha upper limit <=100 MG; Buckley+17 <=500 MG vacuum-dipole spin-down upper scale; Katz+17 abstract ~100 MG but Table 1 Bp=1.1e9–3.6e9*csc(theta) G and mu=4.3e34–1.5e35*csc(theta) G cm3 for mass alternatives; Lyutikov+20 ~1 MG propeller model; Barrett+25 body/Table local ~43-G field and modeled ~15-MG pole if corrected as printed. References listed.
issues.why_it_matters: A single catalogued field or moment would conflate a photospheric upper limit, polar field, local emission-region model and theoretical torque estimates.
issues.needed_action: No single WD field or moment is designated as measured. Verify the Barrett unit issue; retain all other model branches with geometry/mass/torque assumptions, and confirm any use of a preferred field/moment in downstream science.

issues.competing_evidence: Marsh+16 report no clear accretion-disc/broad-line evidence and spin-down-powered energetics; Pelisoli+22 finds the donor close to Roche-lobe filling; Lyutikov+20 proposes a transient low-field propeller with mass loading; Barrett+25 argues for a temporarily ceased accretion/IP-like phase; Buckley+26 describes detached or nearly detached WDP binaries.
issues.why_it_matters: The state classification affects whether a binary-evolution connection is claimed; none of these observations establishes one unique evolutionary path.
issues.needed_action: Keep WDP as the observed class. For a database-level detached/semi-detached flag, decide whether to leave it unresolved pending the forthcoming 2020 multiwavelength primary papers; do not promote a proposed IP/polar/LPT evolutionary pathway.

issues.competing_evidence: Buckley+26 conference proceedings report coherent NICER spin pulsations, L-band MeerKAT variable/polarized emission closer to spin modulation, and a recent rotational Fermi-LAT signal. issues.why_it_matters: New high-energy/radio pulses would add an independent emission component and may alter mechanism interpretation; secondary summaries are insufficient for adoption.
issues.needed_action: Locate and inspect the promised primary NICER/MeerKAT/Fermi papers or data release; until verified, record only the proceedings report and do not mark gamma-ray detection confirmed.
